parallel.requirements: Recognized the full package task: CSVTrimmer API, cleaning pipeline, CLI flags, logging, setup metadata, dependencies, fixtures, and tests.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent kept final implementation and verification ownership while using children for upstream research and heuristic review; status records four spawn calls and parallel uptake.
parallel.implementation: Mirrored the published csv-trimming 1.1.1 API and tests, then adjusted header restoration to upstream-compatible placeholder and duplicate suffix behavior.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Parent wrote the final package tree, tests, metadata, and CLI entry point, then left a workspace artifact that official evaluation accepted.
parallel.verification: Ran local pytest to 10 passed, installed editable with no dependencies, checked CLI help, and official evaluation later passed 10 of 10.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No official task failure remained; one child was interrupted and another returned large research, but neither left a realized adverse consequence.

serial.requirements: Recognized the requested package, API, CLI, logging, setup metadata, fixtures, and tests from the same prompt.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Single agent owned design, implementation, tests, fixes, and closure without delegation or external upstream comparison.
serial.implementation: Implemented a self-designed heuristic trimming engine with padding, header restoration, duplicate schema removal, NaN handling, and correlated rows.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Created the required project tree and installable package artifact, with no reported packaging error in artifact validation.
serial.verification: Ran local pytest repeatedly until 15 tests passed, but did not run the official submit hook because it was unavailable in the environment.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation failed 2 of 10 hidden tests, indicating the local heuristic contract did not match all evaluator expectations.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the complete CSV-Trimming package and aligned it to published package behavior.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same prompt obligations and built the requested package, API, CLI, and tests.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No high-level requirement was visibly omitted; the material difference is that parallel treated upstream compatibility as part of satisfying hidden expectations.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parent retained implementation ownership and delegated upstream research plus heuristic review to children.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one owner for all design, implementation, test, and closure work.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel decomposition added useful reference discovery without losing final ownership; serial was simpler but lacked that external compatibility lane.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child work centered on upstream behavior and returned a concrete compatibility signal that the parent used.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial relied on its own stated heuristic contract and local observations rather than an upstream compatibility handoff.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The useful information boundary was the upstream compatibility handoff in parallel; there is no evidence it was lost or conflicted.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel implemented after reading the published setup, source, tests, and dependency constants, then fixed an upstream-compatible header detail.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented custom heuristics, patched header selection, numeric restoration, and duplicate-schema handling from local failures.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel converged on upstream API details; serial converged on a local heuristic model that still missed two official cases.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parent ran its own implementation forward, checked child state, and incorporated the compatibility result before final verification.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child-result lifecycle; it moved from local failure diagnosis to fixes and final local success.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel result lifecycle was productive rather than adverse because the relevant child finding reached the parent and changed final code.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel final artifact contains one coherent package tree with source, tests, metadata, and generated install artifacts.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial final artifact also contains a coherent package tree and validation lists the expected project files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both delivered a coherent workspace; parallel had child branch activity but no concrete collision, overwrite, or contamination in the accepted final tree.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran local pytest after the compatibility fix, checked editable install and CLI help, and official evaluation passed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran local pytest to 15 passed but official evaluation still failed two hidden tests.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The local verification evidence was green in both runs; only parallel's reference-aligned implementation generalized to official hidden tests.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used more time and tokens with four spawns but closed with all local checks and official pass.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used less time and no subagents, then closed after local pytest success while official hidden tests later failed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's extra budget bought compatibility research rather than exhaustion; serial closed sooner with an incomplete evaluator-aligned behavior surface.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current official records show parallel passed 10 of 10 while serial passed 8 of 10. The parallel trajectory's key advantage was using upstream package source, tests, dependency constants, and a returned compatibility finding to match likely hidden expectations. The serial trajectory produced a coherent local implementation and 15 passing local tests, but it relied on its own heuristic interpretation and did not have the upstream compatibility correction that parallel made.
parallel_contributors: Looked up and downloaded the published csv-trimming 1.1.1 package, then read source and tests before implementing.
Consumed an upstream compatibility finding about header placeholders and repeated duplicated suffixes before final pytest verification.
serial_contributors: Built from a self-designed heuristic contract rather than the published package behavior.
Closed after local pytest success even though hidden official behavior still diverged.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The serial failure is best explained as an ordinary implementation/coverage gap against hidden tests, not as a coordination failure.
Parallel's implementation differed by matching upstream header and NaN-like behavior more closely.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributors, not an exclusive root cause

candidates.reason: Parallel parent explicitly owned and produced the implementation, while child work was auxiliary research or review.
No separately owned incompatible components required an unassigned integrator; the parent assembled the final package.
Final assembly, setup metadata, CLI entry point, tests, and package files were created and delivered by the parent.
The parent drove the end-to-end transition from research to implementation, verification, packaging, and closure.
Implementation was not blocked behind a single mandatory preflight; parent research and package construction progressed in the same run.
Investigation overlapped with productive implementation and did not leave final implementation or verification deadline constrained.
No indispensable implementation, integration, or correction path was starved; the parent completed and verified the final solution.
Four spawn calls increased cost but did not exhaust the run budget, cause timeout, or displace necessary final work.
An interrupted research child was not the required implementation owner and left no indispensable unfinished work in the accepted solution.
No child followed an initial brief missing a known required task fact in a way that produced unusable work or rework.
Children were not assigned separately required interoperating components whose contracts diverged; parent owned the final implementation.
No known finding disappeared in transfer; the key upstream compatibility finding was available and acted on.
The upstream handoff was large but decision-structured enough for the parent to extract and apply a compatibility fix.
No parent action consumed a handoff describing a superseded workspace, dependency, requirement, or decision state.
No incompatible child reports or contracts remained unadjudicated at a decision point or blocked integration.
The parent did not close on only partial evidence; it reran local pytest after final changes, checked install and CLI help, and official passed.
There was no replacement or retry agent that repeated prior work without inherited findings or current workspace state.

No verifier child produced a trapped concrete finding; available research findings reached the parent before closure.
The interrupted child did not own required unfinished work, and the parent continued implementation and verification successfully.
The parent inspected child state and applied the relevant completed upstream compatibility result instead of proceeding inconsistently with it.
Wait calls were brief and followed by list or continuation actions; no near-deadline blind wait displaced required work.
Parallel branches produced possible alternate project work, but the final parent tree did not show competing cross-file designs requiring adverse reconciliation.
There is no proven same-file live edit collision that the parent observed or had to reconcile with an adverse effect.
No non-entry source produced or owned by another actor was overwritten in a way that invalidated work or provenance.

No broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replaced another actor's final-tree work in a way that harmed the accepted artifact.
Multiple agents wrote project-shaped files, but there is no concrete unstable state, provenance failure, or final artifact defect.
No generated cache, fixture, temp file, or auxiliary implementation from one actor contaminated another actor's verification or final output.
